analysis:
MARKET & PORTFOLIO REVIEW — September 4, 2026. Market regime is a confirmed uptrend (+2.3% vs SMA50, positive slope), which is constructive for existing longs. However, the honest assessment of this portfolio's performance demands sobriety: 11.1% win rate, profit factor 0.05x, and Sortino of -4.98 are deeply negative signals. The system is not generating alpha; it is destroying it relative to passive SPY. Two urgent position-level concerns must be addressed.

1) AMP IS OVER-CONCENTRATED: 55 shares at $565.08 = $31,079, representing ~30.8% of equity — a clear violation of the 25% hard cap. This position grew beyond the cap through price appreciation. Action required: Manually sell 11 shares of AMP (~$6,200) to bring concentration to ~24.9%. AMP is up 4.49% so this is a good spot to trim. Thesis (wealth management compounder) remains intact — this is purely a risk-management trim, not an exit. Do this regardless of today's trade decision.

2) IDXX MONITORING: Down 5.09% from entry ($558.52 → $530.10). Thesis (veterinary diagnostics monopoly) remains intact fundamentally, but the position is underwater and must be watched closely. Stop should be defined at ~1.5–2x ATR below entry (ATR ~3% of price, so stop ~$474–$492). Current price is not yet at stop level, but any further deterioration or thesis break (e.g., pricing pressure from corporate vet consolidation, volume softness) warrants exit. No action today.

AON, MCO, ROP: All modestly positive, theses intact, no action needed.

NEW TRADE CAPACITY: After the AMP trim, headroom expands to ~$18,800. With 5 positions already open (at or near the 3–5 position guideline), adding a 6th is borderline. However, given the limited headroom and the sector that would be added (healthcare — diversifying from the financial-heavy book), one disciplined small position in ReMed is justifiable. The setup is the cleanest basing pattern in the healthcare space: uptrend confirmed, 48% of 52w range (not extended), SMA50 slope +7.3%, ATR-based stop produces a 5.6% risk with 2.8x R/R to target. Position will be sized conservatively at ~$12,600 (post-trim headroom), representing ~12% of equity. Worst-case risk is 0.7% of total equity — appropriate given the account's poor track record and the need to preserve capital above all else. Conviction is moderate (62/100) — not forcing alpha, but this is a quality business at a fair price with a confirmed technical setup. Remaining book: AMP (trim to 25%), AON, IDXX, MCO, ROP + RMD = 6 positions — at the outer edge; no further new trades unless a position is exited.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $229.00 or better. Accept a pullback to the $222–$225 zone (near SMA50) as an even better entry if offered. Do not chase above $234 (adds to ATR risk without improving setup).
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: ResMed is the dominant global player in CPAP devices and cloud-connected respiratory care software. The GLP-1 / Ozempic overhang that crushed the stock from $280+ to $182 in 2023–24 is now largely digested — clinical evidence increasingly shows GLP-1 and CPAP are complementary rather than substitutive for sleep apnea patients. Revenue growing +8.6%, operating margin 30.9%, ROE 24.3%, D/E of only 12.5x (extremely low vs peers), FCF $939M, and forward P/E of 17.4x is undemanding for this quality profile. Analyst EPS revisions neutral-to-slightly-positive (+0.5%), meaning the earnings bar is not yet raised. TECHNICAL: Confirmed uptrend basing at 48% of 52-week range — the Stage 1-to-2 transition Weinstein identifies as highest R/R. SMA50 slope +7.3% (accelerating). Price +7% vs SMA50 — extended enough to confirm momentum, not so extended as to be chasing. Entry at current levels puts stop 2.0x ATR below at $216.35, which is well-defined support. Target of $265 is 85% of the way back to the 52-week high ($280), a conservative recovery assumption. R/R = 2.79x.
trades.exit_plan: Primary stops: (1) Hard stop hit at $216.35 — no exceptions. Secondary exits: (2) Earnings miss on Oct 29 with guidance cut or margin compression — exit within 2 sessions regardless of price; (3) Clinical evidence emerges that GLP-1 therapy materially substitutes CPAP adoption at scale — thesis-break exit; (4) Price closes below SMA50 for 3 consecutive sessions with negative slope — trend failure exit. If thesis intact at 12-month mark, evaluate for LTCG conversion to avoid short-term tax drag.
